hypotheses.reasoning: Logins were healthy until 22:44 (e.g. #74, #79: auth-svc token issuance 34-63ms). From 22:44:19 the third-party identity provider (idp.example/oauth2/token) became slow (4.2s, 7.7s) and then hit full 30s timeouts (#84, #97). auth-svc hangs on the IdP, so account-svc AuthClient.issueToken times out (#85, #98). The 30s calls fill account-svc's HTTP pool to auth-svc (#101 50/50, #108 checkout timeouts), which produces the 503s at edge-proxy on POST /login (#96, #106, #114, #117). There was no deploy or config change, and the DB, cache and audit-consumer were healthy. The fault starts at the external provider.

The same lines can be read as a dependency timeout: the failures show up as 30s upstream timeouts, and there is no long 30s timeout ceiling or circuit breaker on the IdP call. But the slow dependency is an outside provider whose latency got worse over time, not an internal service.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the IdP provider's status page and contact the vendor. In auth-svc, cut the IdP call timeout from 30s to a few seconds and add a circuit breaker so it fails fast and doesn't fill account-svc's connection pool. If allowed, accept cached tokens or sessions for a grace period, and fail over to a backup IdP region if there is one.
